back: Nodes (vertices) joined by edges; weighted if each edge has a cost, directed if edges go one way.
Finds the shortest distance from a start node to all others by repeatedly visiting the unvisited node with the smallest distance and updating its neighbours.
Expands the open node with the lowest f = g + h to find a shortest path to one goal.
An estimate of the remaining cost to the goal; admissible if it never overestimates.
g: cost from the start so far; h: estimated cost to the goal; f: estimated total cost through the node.
Open: nodes reached but not expanded. Closed: nodes already expanded.
Follow the previous node from the destination back to the start and reverse it.
A* uses a heuristic, searches towards one goal and usually expands fewer nodes; with h = 0 it behaves like Dijkstra.
